name: Arming Sword
description: The plain one-handed sword of the European knight, made in their thousands at Passau and Solingen. Reliable in the hand and easily repaired.

name: Bastard Sword
description: A long hand-and-a-half blade, many of them brought to Malta from the Order's commanderies in France and Provence.

name: Mace & Shield
description: A flanged mace with a round steel shield, as carried by the Order's galley soldiers in boarding fights.

name: Pike
description: A long ash shaft with a steel head, the backbone of the Spanish tercios. Kept in the Birgu armoury by the hundred.

name: Arquebus
description: A matchlock arquebus, mostly from Spanish and Sicilian workshops. Slow to load but deadly behind a parapet.

name: Boat Hook
description: A harbour hook used to pull boats to the quays of Birgu and Senglea, here pressed into service as a weapon.

name: Kilij
description: The curved Ottoman sabre, its broad tip shaped for drawing cuts. Forged in Istanbul and Bursa.

name: Tüfek
description: The Ottoman matchlock musket, long-barrelled and well balanced, the pride of the janissary ortas.

name: Sipahi Lance
description: A light cavalry lance with a pennant, carried by the timar-holding horsemen of the provinces.

name: Grenado Sling
description: A sling for throwing clay and iron bombs, the tool of the Ottoman bombardiers.

name: Cutlass
description: A short, heavy sailor's blade from a North African workshop, ideal in a crowded galley.

name: Swivel Gun
description: A small breech-loading gun normally mounted on a galley's rail, here bolted onto an armatura.

name: Ram-Arm
description: A battering-ram arm built into Scala's machines, its iron head driven by steam.

name: Colossus Cannon
description: A giant cannon cast for Scala's Colossus, too heavy for any ordinary harness.

name: Tower Guns
description: A row of light guns mounted on the siege tower's upper platform.

name: Falchion
description: A broad single-edged cutting blade, heavy at the tip, favoured by knights and sergeants of the Order alike.

name: War Hammer
description: A Milanese horseman's hammer with a spike opposite, made to burst plate armour.

name: Partisan
description: A broad-bladed spear of Italian design, carried by officers and bodyguards of the Grand Master.

name: Wheellock Musket
description: A German wheellock musket, its clockwork lock firing without a lit match. Expensive and highly prized.

name: Yatağan
description: The forward-curved Ottoman short sword, favoured by janissaries for close fighting.

name: Long Tüfek
description: An extra-long tüfek built for marksmen, accurate at ranges no ordinary musket can match.

name: Milanese Spada
description: Forged in the Milanese workshops of the Missaglia tradition and bought by a Provençal knight before sailing to Malta. Its temper holds an edge through a whole day's fighting.

name: Toledo Espada
description: A Toledo blade quenched in the waters of the Tagus and sent to the Order as a gift from the Viceroy of Sicily. Light, flexible and almost impossible to break.

name: Venetian Corsesca
description: A three-pronged spear from the Venetian Arsenal, its side blades made to catch and turn an enemy's weapon. Bought from a galley captain at Birgu.

name: Nuremberg Halberd
description: An etched and gilded halberd from a Nuremberg master smith, made for the guard of a German commandery. It combines axe, spike and hook in perfect balance.

name: Brescian Arquebus
description: Gardone in Val Trompia, near Brescia, bored its barrels straighter than any other town. This arquebus throws its ball true at long range.

name: Augsburg Petronel
description: A wheellock petronel from Augsburg with an ivory-inlaid stock and a clockwork lock that never misfires. A treasure that only a Grand Cross could afford.

name: Birgu Flanged Mace
description: Forged at a Maltese workshop below Fort St Angelo from Sicilian iron. Its seven flanges cut through mail and dent plate.

name: Milanese Horseman's Hammer
description: A hammer from the Negroli workshop in Milan, its head etched with saints and its spike tempered to punch through plate. A favourite of knights who fought at Tunis.

name: Bursa Yatağan
description: A yatağan forged in Bursa with a bone grip and a forward-curving blade. Its smith marked it with a crescent stamp.

name: Damascene Kilij
description: A kilij of watered steel from Damascus, its blade showing patterns like flowing water and inlaid in gold with verses. Worthy of an ağa.

name: Akıncı Mızrak
description: A long raiding lance of the frontier cavalry, its head forged in Edirne. Light and fast in the hands of a skilled rider.

name: Silahdar's Teber
description: A long-hafted axe from the palace workshops of Istanbul, carried by the Sultan's weapon-bearers. Its crescent blade is inlaid in silver.

name: Edirne Tüfek
description: A tüfek from the Edirne gunsmiths, with a heavy damascened barrel and coral-inlaid stock. More reliable than standard issue.

name: Istanbul Long Tüfek
description: A long-barrelled tüfek from the imperial arsenal at Istanbul, bored true and fitted for a marksman: it reaches further than any common gun.

name: Humbara Pot
description: Glazed clay bombs packed with powder and naphtha by the humbaracı corps. They burst in a sheet of flame.

name: Tophane Bronze Humbara
description: Bronze shells cast at the Tophane foundry of Istanbul alongside the great siege guns. They burst into deadly fragments.

name: Djerba Boarding Pike
description: A hooked boarding pike taken from a Spanish galley at Djerba in 1560 and rehafted by Algerian corsairs. It drags men off decks and walls alike.

name: Silver Gürz
description: A flanged mace of a pasha's guard, its steel head chased with silver. A badge of rank and a crushing weapon.
